candidates.title: Review low-value pages for removal

demandEvidence.chore: Review existing site pages for whether they answer a question or solve a problem, then remove pages that do neither.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: If it does not answer a question or solve something, I delete it.

candidates.whoPays: Hypothesis: small freelance web studios maintaining client sites may pay for a page-upkeep review assistant.

experimentPlan.output: A review table marking each supplied page as keep, review, or possible removal with a short reason tied to the supplied page purpose.
inputs: Synthetic page title and URL label
Operator supplied audience question or task
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a small list of pages for a periodic upkeep review.
steps: Collect page labels and operator supplied purpose notes.
Compare each purpose note with the stated audience question or task.
Draft a keep, review, or possible removal label with a reason.
Flag missing purpose information instead of guessing.
Ask a person to verify each suggestion before any page is changed.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a fixed synthetic list, verify every output row maps to one input page, missing purpose notes are flagged, and no page is changed automatically.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator supplies context and confirms whether a page should remain; the prototype never accesses or edits a live site.
unverified: Whether page-purpose labels predict useful content
Whether a repeated upkeep workflow exists among small studios
Any automated website access or editing capability

ease.reason: The post describes a simple page-purpose review, but no supplied implementation reference documents an automated version.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small web studios may pay to reduce page upkeep; this tip shows no buying intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic page-list prototype is bounded; real site access and useful page judgments remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A repeatable page review can produce suggestions, but no automation capability is documented and a person must decide removals.

evidence.reason: The retained native span gives a concrete keep-or-delete rule, but frequency, fields and corroborated demand are unknown.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the span supports a bounded manual page-review chore, but no implementation support is supplied and the buyer and repeat frequency are unverified.

candidates.title: Summarize long email threads for review

demandEvidence.chore: Summarize long email conversations into a compact history and draft prefill for a person to review.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: To save email resume properly, i need immutable id to reference original email of the resume.

candidates.whoPays: Hypothesis: small professional-services firms handling long client email threads may pay for review-ready summaries.

experimentPlan.output: A compact summary of a fictional email thread with the latest request, relevant prior context, and a draft response prefill for human review.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator pastes a fictional or otherwise approved thread for a summary draft.
steps: Read the supplied thread in chronological order.
Identify the latest request and relevant earlier context.
Draft a compact summary and response prefill.
Flag ambiguous references or missing context.
Return the draft for a person to correct and approve.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a fixed set of fictional threads, check that each output preserves the latest request, does not invent facts, and flags deliberately ambiguous references.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies approved text, verifies every detail, and decides whether to use any draft; the experiment does not connect to a mailbox or send email.
unverified: Summary accuracy on varied real conversations
Mailbox access, permissions and privacy controls
Whether compact history reduces review effort for the proposed buyer

ease.reason: The post describes the desired summary output, but no supplied implementation reference supports email intake or summarization.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small service firms may pay to reduce thread review time; this request does not establish buying intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can use operator-supplied fictional threads; secure mailbox access and summary accuracy remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A draft summary is repeatable, but no implementation capability is documented and a person must review it before use.

evidence.reason: The retained span describes long email conversations, compact history and draft prefill, but not frequency or corroborated demand.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: a concrete summarization task is stated, but the supplied spans do not support a safe email integration or reliable summaries; buyer demand remains a hypothesis.

candidates.title: Draft booking and service status alerts

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare booking confirmations, provider assignment notices, payment-status updates, and customer alerts for an on-demand service workflow.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: booking confirmations, provider assignment notifications, payment status updates, and customer alerts

candidates.whoPays: Hypothesis: small on-demand service operators may pay for help preparing booking and status notices.

experimentPlan.output: A proposed event review sheet with one draft booking or status notice and a missing-information flag for each synthetic event.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator provides a synthetic booking or status event for a draft notice.
steps: Read the event fields supplied by the operator.
Check whether required notice details are present.
Draft the matching confirmation or status message from the approved template.
Flag missing or conflicting fields without inferring payment or assignment success.
Return the draft for human review and sending.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For synthetic events with known missing and conflicting fields, verify the prototype flags them and drafts no unsupported success statement.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies events and templates, confirms payment and assignment facts, and approves and sends every message.
unverified: Access to actual booking or payment systems
Webhook delivery, retry and duplicate prevention mechanics
Notice accuracy and business value across real operator workflows

ease.reason: The post names notification tasks, but no supplied implementation reference supports webhooks, APIs or message delivery.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small on-demand service operators may pay to reduce notice handling; this discussion shows no purchase or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can draft notices from synthetic events; integration, retries and duplicate prevention remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: Event-to-draft steps could repeat, but no implementation capability is documented and a person must verify and send notices.

evidence.reason: The retained span names booking, assignment, payment-status and customer notices plus failure concerns, but no fields or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the post specifies several notification tasks, but no implementation evidence supports external APIs, retries or delivery; payment and buyer demand are unverified.
